title: OIDC rediscovery refreshes the discovery document only; the exchanged session survives it, and discovery is single-flight
current_state: 11 of 12 still lose the session. java OpenIdConnectAuthenticator.java:116/126 builds a new OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator (new OAuth2TokenManager, tokenExchanged=false) once discoveryExpiry passes; getDelegate is synchronized (single-flight). kotlin OpenIdConnectAuthenticator.kt:~120 same, no lock. csharp OpenIdConnectAuthenticator.cs:108 same, no lock. php OpenIdConnectAuthenticator.php:163 same, no lock. python openid_connect_authenticator.py:154 same, no lock. ruby openid_connect_authenticator.rb:131 same, no lock. node openid-connect-authenticator.ts:150 same, no in-flight promise. dart openid_connect_authenticator.dart:158 same, no in-flight future. go openid_connect_authenticator.go:210 same, mutex held across the fetch. rust openid_connect_authenticator.rs:242 swaps in a fresh Arc delegate (fresh manager, token_exchanged=false); only guards a concurrent install. swift OpenIdConnectAuthenticator.swift:180 same, lock only around the state write, not around the fetch. elixir openid_connect_authenticator.ex:265 keep_token_manager/2 re-uses the previous delegate's token manager (tokens + mark_exchanged flag) across rediscovery, i.e. already correct for state (test openid_connect_authenticator_test.exs:343), fetch not serialised. Effect in the 11: after max-age (86400 s default; max-age=0 means the very first call after exchangeCode) getAuthHeaders throws 'Must call exchangeCode() before making API requests' and the user must re-authorise. No language tests max-age/rediscovery except elixir.
canonical: The session (access token, refresh token, 'exchanged' flag) is owned by the OAuth2TokenManager, which outlives discovery. (1) Move the 'exchanged' flag into OAuth2TokenManager (markExchanged/isExchanged, exactly as elixir already has it); OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator.getAuthHeaders reads it from the manager. (2) Give OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator an internal constructor/overload that takes an existing token manager; on rediscovery the OIDC authenticator builds the replacement delegate around the previous delegate's manager (new authorization/token endpoints, same session). (3) If rediscovery fails (non-2xx, transport, malformed document) the old delegate and its expiry are left untouched, the error propagates and the next call retries (no stale serving, no silent swallow). (4) Discovery fetch is single-flight per authenticator using the language's idiom (lock / in-flight future), re-checking expiry inside it. PHP is the FORCED exception for (4): no in-process concurrency, and the token manager already documents cross-process locking as out of scope. The max-age value is clamped per the expires_in/max-age decision. Standing AGENTS.md rules are not touched; the 'RFC 8414 default 86400' behaviour stays.
alternatives: (a) Mutate endpoints in place on the existing delegate: needs mutable endpoint fields in go/rust/swift/elixir (immutable or Arc'd types), wider surface than sharing the manager. (b) Ignore max-age once a code was exchanged: endpoints could rotate, and it silently changes caching semantics. (c) Serve the stale delegate when rediscovery fails: hides OP outages and security-relevant endpoint changes. (d) Status quo (drop session, force re-login): rejected, it is the bug. (e) Leave single-flight out because state-preserving rebuild makes duplicates harmless: rejected, it still fires duplicate discovery GETs and last-writer races on the first discovery; it is cheap with each language's own primitive.
rationale: Criteria (c) and (b): the session must never be silently discarded by a cache refresh, and elixir (plus java/go for locking) already show the shape is feasible without a new dependency. RFC 8414/OIDC Discovery only describe caching of metadata, never invalidating client authorization state. Rust/kotlin/csharp/swift/node/dart/python/ruby need only stdlib primitives (Mutex, SemaphoreSlim, Task/Future, threading.Lock).

title: Refresh grant carries client authentication (RFC 6749 sec 6 / 3.2.1) and the fallback re-runs the real grant
current_state: Uniform in all 12. Password authenticator (java OAuth2PasswordAuthenticator.java:159-170, kotlin .kt:83-92, csharp .cs:98-109, php .php:138-143, python .py:110-117, ruby .rb:98-105, node .ts:131-136, dart .dart:96-102, go .go:103-108, rust .rs:157-161, swift .swift:90-96, elixir .ex:136-141) builds {grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token} with NO client_id/client_secret once a refresh token exists, with a code comment that misreads RFC 6749 sec 6 ('carries only grant_type and refresh_token'). In BASIC mode the Authorization header still rides along via extraHeaders, in BODY mode the refresh is unauthenticated. The auth-code authenticator (java :168-170, rust :213-218, elixir, ...) always sends the bare refresh params (it has no Basic option). The token managers (java OAuth2TokenManager.java:101-106, go :108-117, rust :150-158) copy client_id/client_secret only from the params they are handed, so nothing is added, and on failure 'fall back to the original grant' re-POSTs the identical bare refresh request (two identical failing requests; the password flow can never re-run the password grant). Manager sends the refresh to the same tokenUrl it was given (the authenticator pre-selects refreshUrl).
canonical: RFC 6749 sec 6: a client that authenticated at the token endpoint authenticates the refresh the same way (sec 3.2.1). (1) Token managers gain an optional refreshUrl argument on getAccessToken (default = tokenUrl). (2) Password authenticator no longer branches on refresh-token presence: it always passes the password-grant params (client_id/client_secret only in BODY mode, Basic header via extraHeaders otherwise) with tokenUrl and refreshUrl. The manager, when it holds a refresh token and params.grant_type != refresh_token, POSTs {grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret (copied from params, i.e. BODY mode only)} plus the same extraHeaders to refreshUrl; on any non-cancellation failure it falls back to POSTing the original params to tokenUrl (re-runs the password grant, as the client-credentials flow already does). (3) Auth-code authenticator passes {grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret} with the refresh endpoint as the url; when params.grant_type is already refresh_token the manager performs exactly one POST (no internal refresh attempt, no duplicate fallback), so a rejected refresh surfaces as OAuth2ServerError once. No scope on refresh (optional per sec 6).
alternatives: (a) Only add client_id/secret to the refresh params and keep the duplicate fallback: fixes the first half of the finding but leaves password flows unable to re-login and sends a duplicate failing request. (b) Add a ClientAuthMethod to auth-code: scope creep, the spec/generator has no such option for that flow. (c) Leave as is because 'matches the other SDKs': it is uniformly wrong against Keycloak/Google/Auth0 confidential clients, and uniform bugs are not a parity argument.
rationale: (a) RFC 6749 sec 6 literally says a confidential client or a client issued credentials MUST authenticate per sec 3.2.1; (c) the current behaviour makes every flow with a refresh_token break permanently at first expiry against such OPs with no recovery path (invalidateAccessToken never clears the refresh token); (d) only parameter plumbing, no new dependency.

title: exchangeCode always POSTs the authorization_code grant and replaces the session; it never goes through the token cache or the refresh path
current_state: Uniform in all 12. exchangeCode builds {grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri} and calls the caching tokenManager.getAccessToken (java OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator.java:153, go oauth2_authorization_code_authenticator.go:145, rust .rs:144, elixir .ex:179, python/ruby/node/dart/php/kotlin/csharp/swift equivalents). That method first returns a still-valid cached token and otherwise tries the stored refresh_token grant (java OAuth2TokenManager.java:92-117), so a second exchangeCode (re-login, account switch, scope upgrade) never sends the new code and still sets the exchanged flag; an old refresh_token also survives a response that has none.
canonical: Add an explicit exchange operation to the token manager (java exchange(tokenUrl, params, extraHeaders)) that: takes the manager lock, saves the previous access/refresh/expiry, clears them, POSTs the given params verbatim to the given URL (no cache hit, no refresh attempt), on success keeps exactly what the response carried (a response without refresh_token leaves NO refresh token; without expires_in leaves no expiry) and marks the session exchanged (flag lives in the manager, see the rediscovery decision); on any failure restores the previous state and rethrows, so a mistyped code does not log the user out. exchangeCode in the auth-code authenticator (and therefore the OIDC delegate) calls only this operation. getAuthHeaders is unchanged. Client-credentials/password flows keep the caching getAccessToken.
alternatives: (a) Call invalidateAccessToken + clear refresh token before getAccessToken: leaves the refresh-first branch live and wipes the old session even when the new exchange fails. (b) Make exchangeCode throw if already exchanged: breaks legitimate re-login on a long-lived authenticator. (c) Leave as is: silently keeps the previous identity, a correctness and security-relevant bug.
rationale: (a) RFC 6749 sec 4.1.3: the token request for an authorization_code grant must carry the code; a client method named exchangeCode that skips the request violates its contract. (c) caller-safe: failure restores state, success fully replaces it. (d) pure plumbing in the manager of each language.

title: Per-scheme OAuth wrappers pass the spec's declared scopes, in spec declaration order
current_state: F018 is FIXED: go (machine_auth_client_credentials_authenticator.go:~25 []string{"pets:write","pets:read"}), rust (machine_auth_client_credentials_authenticator.rs:22-24) and elixir (...ex:23) now pass the scopes, and tests pin it (go oauth2_client_credentials_authenticator_test.go:89-105 'scope=pets%3Awrite+pets%3Aread', rust ...test.rs:291-306, elixir ...test.exs:50-58). F288 is STILL TRUE in all 12: AbstractBetterCodegen.java:1137 copies flow.getScopes() (swagger-parser Scopes extends LinkedHashMap, spec order pets:read, pets:write at petstore openapi.yaml:1470-1472 and :1488-1490) into new HashMap<>, so every wrapper emits ["pets:write","pets:read"] and the scope= string on the wire is in hash order. Every per-language formatXScopes (e.g. BetterJavaCodegen.java:955 scopes.keySet()) then preserves that wrong order.
canonical: Wrappers carry the scheme's scopes in the order the spec declares them. SchemeAuthSpec stores scopes in a LinkedHashMap (Collections.unmodifiableMap(new LinkedHashMap<>(scopes))). Single generator fix, no per-language template change; all 12 follow automatically. Scope = all scopes the scheme declares (as today); per-operation `security` requirement scopes remain unused (unchanged, not part of this decision). Goldens: pets:read before pets:write.
alternatives: Sort scopes alphabetically: deterministic but discards the spec author's order and still changes the wire string vs. what the spec shows. Keep HashMap and document: nondeterministic across JDKs for large maps, and unrelated to the spec.
rationale: (a) OpenAPI scopes is an ordered map in the parsed model and the scope parameter is a space-delimited list where authors expect declaration order (RFC 6749 sec 3.3 treats it as unordered but byte-identical output across runs/SDKs is the repo rule); (c) no semantic change for the OP; (d) one-line generator change.

title: OpenID Connect authenticators always request the openid scope
current_state: Uniform in all 12. title: expires_in and discovery max-age: one decimal grammar for strings and a one-year ceiling applied before any date arithmetic
current_state: F116 (partly fixed): only rust clamps (oauth2_token_manager.rs:31 MAX_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS=31_536_000 applied at :268; openid_connect_authenticator.rs:52 parse_max_age clamps to one year; test at openid_connect_authenticator_test.rs:450-455 max-age=18446744073709551615). Still unclamped: swift (OAuth2TokenManager.swift:356/361 Int(d.rounded(.down)) TRAPS for >= 9.22e18, e.g. expires_in 1e20), java (OAuth2TokenManager.java:302-316 returns Long.MAX_VALUE then Instant.plusSeconds throws ArithmeticException/DateTimeException at :123-ish; OIDC parseMaxAge likewise), csharp (.cs:294 AddSeconds throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException; ParseMaxAge long.TryParse overflow falls to default), kotlin (.kt:256 (expiresIn-bufferSecs)*1000L overflows -> expiry in the past -> refetch every call; OIDC plusSeconds throws), go (.go:232 time.Duration(n)*time.Second overflows above ~9.2e9 s; int64(math.Floor(1e20)) is implementation-defined; parseDiscoveryMaxAge Atoi), dart (.dart:216 Duration(seconds:) microsecond overflow; int.tryParse fallback to default), ruby (digits-only grammar fixed the Float('1e400') crash but huge Integer still unbounded), php/python/node/elixir (no crash, but php (int)floor(1e20) is undefined and python float+int can OverflowError for 400-digit max-age). F294 (string grammar) is fixed only in java (text.matches \\d+(\\.\\d+)?), ruby (regex), node (regex), swift (regex, but allows a trailing dot '5.'): kotlin toDoubleOrNull (hex/p-exponent, 'd'/'f' suffix), csharp double.TryParse(NumberStyles.Float) (exponent, sign), php is_numeric (exponent, leading whitespace), python float() (exponent, underscores '3_600'), dart double.tryParse (hex '0x10', exponent), go strconv.ParseFloat (exponent, 'Inf'), rust str::parse::<f64> (exponent, 'inf'), elixir Integer.parse/Float.parse (exponent) still use their native grammar.
canonical: (1) String expires_in: trim ASCII whitespace, then require ^[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$ (floor the fraction); anything else (hex, exponent, sign, suffix, underscore, NaN/Inf, trailing dot) is unusable -> 0 -> token stale (refetch next call), as java/ruby/node do. JSON numbers keep floor() and non-finite -> stale. (2) A shared ceiling constant of 31_536_000 seconds (one year, rust's existing value) applied to the parsed expires_in and to the parsed discovery max-age BEFORE subtracting the 30 s buffer, multiplying to ms or adding to a clock; digits that overflow the language integer saturate to the ceiling (not to the 86400 default). A huge-but-finite lifetime therefore caches for at most a year (no throw, no wrap, no trap); a non-finite or non-positive one stays 'stale'. Applies in all 12 even where nothing crashes today (php, python, node, elixir) so behaviour is identical.
alternatives: Treat huge values as stale/unusable: avoids caching a token for a year but makes a server that legitimately sends 'never expires' style 2^53 values refetch on every call. Different ceilings per language: no, rust's already tested constant is reusable everywhere. Keep each language's native numeric grammar and only clamp: leaves the F294 split ('0x10' = 16 s in dart, 0 elsewhere).
rationale: (a) RFC 6749 sec 5.1 defines expires_in as a lifetime in seconds (a number); server input must not crash the client (error-contract); (b) java/ruby/node/swift already use the strict grammar and rust already clamps; (c) no process trap/silent wrap; (d) all stdlib.

title: Token-request body and authorize-URL parameters are emitted in one fixed order
current_state: Insertion-ordered and mutually identical: kotlin (mutableMapOf), csharp (Dictionary, insertion order while nothing is removed), php, python, ruby, node, dart. Not deterministic or not the same: java builds params with HashMap (OAuth2ClientCredentialsAuthenticator.java:88, OAuth2PasswordAuthenticator.java:~150, OAuth2AuthorizationCodeAuthenticator.java:146, manager refreshParams :96) so the body is grant_type, scope, client_secret, client_id (hash order); go oauth2_token_manager.go:170 url.Values.Encode() sorts keys, and go's authorize URLs (oauth2_authorization_code_authenticator.go:123, oauth2_implicit_authenticator.go) use params.Encode() sorted (client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, state); elixir oauth2_token_manager.ex:184 URI.encode_query(map) sorted, authorize URL ex:144 sorted; rust oauth2_token_manager.rs:192 iterates a HashMap with RandomState (different order per process); swift OAuth2TokenManager.swift:208 params.map over a Dictionary (per-process seeded). rust and swift authorize URLs are built as ordered lists and java builds the authorize URL in code order, so those already match.
canonical: The wire order is part of the byte-identical contract. Token body: grant_type, code, refresh_token, username, password, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, scope (then any other key, sorted). That is exactly the insertion order the seven ordered SDKs already produce for client_credentials (grant_type, client_id, client_secret, scope), password (grant_type, username, password, client_id, client_secret, scope), authorization_code (grant_type, code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri) and refresh (grant_type, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret). Authorize URL: response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state (implicit: no redirect_uri). Implementation: java uses LinkedHashMap; go/rust/swift/elixir, whose maps are unordered by contract, serialise through one helper that applies this key priority list (go and elixir build the authorize URL from an ordered list instead of url.Values / URI.encode_query(map)).
alternatives: Change the callers to ordered containers everywhere (ordered slice of pairs in go, Vec in rust, KeyValuePairs in swift, keyword lists in elixir): cleaner but changes every token-manager signature in 4 languages. Sort alphabetically everywhere: would change the 7 SDKs that are already insertion-ordered and have tests asserting contains() only.
rationale: (b) majority insertion order; (d) a key-priority helper needs no new dependency and keeps the manager API stable; semantically equivalent for form decoders but required for byte-level assertions and deterministic logs/cassettes.

canonical: Whenever an HTTP response arrived and the SDK then cannot use it, the thrown ApiError/ApiException carries (a) the real status, (b) the real response headers: the same lower-cased map the success path puts in ApiHttpResponse.headers, never null and never a substitute empty map, (c) responseBody/errorBody null (body is unusable by definition), and (d) the underlying failure as cause where one exists. This covers decompression failure and all three redirect refusals in all 12. Null/nil/None headers stay reachable only through the transport-failure constructor, exactly as the AGENTS.md 'responseHeaders null vs empty is a signal' rule says. Constructors must never default headers to an empty map: php ApiException::__construct default becomes null, and node ClientError and every leaf ctor default becomes null.
alternatives: (1) Null headers when the body is unusable: rejected, contradicts AGENTS.md:194-203 and hides x-request-id and retry-after from the caller. (2) Pass an empty map when headers are not at hand: rejected, it is the exact 'default to empty map for consistency' that AGENTS.md forbids. (3) Make decompress failure a transport/Network error: rejected, a response did arrive and the AGENTS rule is that it is an ApiError carrying its status.
rationale: Criterion (a) AGENTS.md:194 (null means no response arrived). (b) python, ruby, go already do this on every path; php, dart, rust do it on decompress. (c) callers that branch on headers == null to decide 'retry transport' vs 'inspect the response' get the correct answer. (d) every language has the response headers in scope at each throw site (verified at each cited line) so no new dependency.

current_state:
F274: each SDK uses its stdlib trim in the api-key and bearer constructors: java Character.isWhitespace/isBlank (BearerAuthenticator.java:23), kotlin isBlank (BearerAuthenticator.kt:24), csharp IsNullOrWhiteSpace, php trim (ApiKeyAuthenticator.php:32; strips NUL, not FF), python str.strip (api_key_authenticator.py:30; bearer_authenticator.py:28), ruby strip (api_key_authenticator.rb:64), node trim, go strings.TrimSpace (bearer_authenticator.go:53), dart trim (api_key_authenticator.dart:40), rust trim (bearer_authenticator.rs:41), swift .whitespacesAndNewlines (ApiKeyAuthenticator.swift:31, BearerAuthenticator.swift:27), elixir String.trim (api_key_authenticator.ex:53, bearer_authenticator.ex:45). Results differ for \f, \x1f, U+00A0, U+0085, NUL (per the ledger probe).
F275: in all 12 the 'Bearer ' prefix de-duplication runs in getAuthHeaders (java BearerAuthenticator.java:55-64, python :43-49, go :89, rust :83-87, elixir :70-82, swift :55-60), after the empty guard, so token 'Bearer ' or 'bearer    ' passes construction and the header becomes 'Authorization: Bearer ' / 'Bearer    ' (credential-less).
canonical: Constructor order for the bearer authenticator: (1) if the token starts with `bearer ` (case-insensitive ASCII, 7 chars) strip that prefix once and store the stripped token; getAuthHeaders then emits `Bearer ` + stored token with no further stripping; (2) reject as `Bearer token must not be empty` when the stored token is empty or consists only of the ASCII whitespace set {U+0020, U+0009, U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D}; (3) then the existing printable-ASCII check. For api keys: reject as `API key value for '<name>' must not be empty` when empty or only that set, then the existing CR/LF/NUL check. The set is implemented as an explicit private helper per language, never the native trim/strip/isBlank. Unicode whitespace (U+00A0, U+0085, U+2028...) is NOT in the set: a key made only of such characters is non-empty for query/cookie locations and is rejected by the existing character checks for header and bearer. NUL-only input is reported as the forbidden-character error in all 12 (php and ruby no longer say 'must not be empty'); '\x1f' is accepted by the emptiness check everywhere (java, kotlin, python no longer reject it as empty) and left to the downstream character checks.
alternatives: Unicode White_Space property: rejected, it needs a 25-code-point table per language, runtimes disagree on membership (U+180E, U+0085), and header/cookie values are ASCII-only on the wire so Unicode whitespace is not the credential-less-header risk. Broaden the forbidden set to all C0 controls: a reasonable follow-up (RFC 9110 field-value forbids CTLs except HTAB) but a separate behaviour change, not needed to unify the emptiness guard. Keep native trims and only document: rejected, results provably differ across 12.
rationale: (a) RFC 9110 s5.5/s5.6.3 treats SP/HTAB (OWS) as the only insignificant whitespace in field values; our set is OWS plus the line/page controls the ledger probe showed disagreement on. (c) closes the F275 hole where the guard exists to prevent 'Authorization: Bearer ' and fails in all 12; the likely real-world trigger is an env var templated as `Bearer ${TOKEN}` with TOKEN unset. (d) explicit loops need no dependency.

current_state: java: Collections.unmodifiableMap(new HashMap<>(headers)) (ApiResult.java:33); csharp: ReadOnlyDictionary over a copy (ApiResult.cs:35-36); rust: private field exposed by shared reference; node: `Readonly<Record>` type only, no runtime copy or freeze (api-result.ts:18); php readonly array and swift struct dictionary and elixir map are value types. title: Binary (format: binary) response: always raw bytes, never JSON-parsed, one rule for JSON / absent / text / binary Content-Type
canonical: A response whose declared return is format:binary (java InputStream, csharp Stream, ruby File/StringIO, kotlin/python/dart/go/rust/swift/elixir/node bytes, php string) is NEVER passed to the JSON parser, whatever the Content-Type. The transport contract is unchanged (text-class media types arrive as decoded text, everything else as base64): (1) Content-Type absent/empty, text/*, application/json, +json, xml or js => the UTF-8 bytes of the body string verbatim (so getPetPhoto answered with application/json {Photo} returns the raw JSON bytes; the caller sees the type via the WithHttpInfo headers/rawBody). (2) Any other Content-Type => base64 body decoded with the SDK's single strict decoder; malformed input raises the SDK serialization error (SerializationException / SerializationError). No 'try base64, else treat as raw text' fallbacks and no silent empty result. To make this possible in the 8 languages whose native type collapses binary and byte, the op template passes the response format to the base layer (e.g. a binaryReturn flag emitted from {{#returnProperty}}{{#isBinary}}, already used by node/apis.mustache:348 and php/api/api.mustache:378), as F150 proposes.
alternatives: Rejected: raise a typed SerializationError when a binary operation receives application/json. It makes a spec-declared success response (getPetPhoto declares application/json) un-receivable, hides the body from the caller and would change java/csharp/ruby/dart which already return the bytes; raw bytes lose nothing because ApiResult keeps headers and rawBody. Rejected: generate a oneOf return type per content type (new codegen model, L effort, not expressible in several of the 12 type systems). Rejected: keep per-language 'base64 first, fall back to text' heuristics (dart, swift, php, csharp, elixir) because valid-base64-looking text is decoded to garbage and a contract violation by a custom ApiClient is hidden.
rationale: (a) OpenAPI says the response schema is chosen per media type, so a JSON reply to getPetPhoto is legal and must not be reinterpreted as an image or rejected; format:binary means 'opaque octets', so the faithful value is the octets that arrived. (b) java, csharp, ruby already return the raw bytes for JSON, kotlin/csharp/ruby/java for absent Content-Type, and java's mirror bug (F153) is already fixed. (c) Of the other behaviours, rust returns Ok(empty Vec) (silent data loss), python/node return a parsed object typed as bytes, php returns the string 'Array'; raw bytes is the only choice that neither throws on a legal reply nor lies about the type. (d) Needs no dependency; only a flag from a field the templates already read.

title: format: byte response (getPetAvatarThumbnail): JSON by default, one strict decoder, every failure is a SerializationError
canonical: A top-level format:byte return (java/kotlin/csharp byte[]/ByteArray, ruby ByteArray, php 'byte', node Buffer closure, python/dart/go/rust/swift/elixir bytes) follows the model-return path: Content-Type absent/empty or JSON mime => JSON-parse the body, require a JSON string, decode it with the SAME strict base64 decoder the SDK already uses for model format:byte fields (padding/alphabet strictness itself is owned by F081, not decided here), return bytes. Any failure (invalid JSON, non-string JSON, malformed base64) raises the SDK's serialization error; none leaks a platform exception (IllegalArgumentException, FormatException) and none returns empty or garbage bytes. A non-JSON Content-Type on a byte return is handled by the non-JSON decision (SerializationError). This is the AGENTS rule 'dart defaults an absent/empty response Content-Type to JSON ... matching swift/node' generalised to all 12, and the AGENTS 'python and node reject malformed base64 on decode' rule extended from model fields to the operation-return path.
alternatives: Rejected: treat an absent Content-Type on a byte return as text and return the UTF-8 bytes (what java/kotlin/csharp do today): the body is a JSON string literal, so the caller receives the quoted base64 text as 'bytes'. Rejected: separate lenient decoder for operation returns; two decoders per SDK would immediately re-diverge.
rationale: (a) The declared schema is application/json carrying a base64 string; decoding it is the only reading that matches OAS format:byte, and the AGENTS standing rules (absent CT = JSON; reject malformed base64; error contract 'every decode failure is a SerializationError'). (b) python, ruby, php, go, swift, elixir already do exactly this. (c) node silently decodes '!!not*base64??' to 6 garbage bytes and rust returns an empty Vec with Ok: silent data change; java/kotlin/csharp/dart give wrong bytes for absent CT. (d) Every SDK already has a strict base64 decoder in its ObjectSerializer.

title: Non-JSON success Content-Type on a non-binary return: String gets the text, everything else is a SerializationError naming the Content-Type
canonical: On a 2xx response with a non-empty body and a return type that is not format:binary: (1) Content-Type absent/empty or JSON mime (incl. +json, vendor) => JSON path (unchanged, and dart/swift/node/go keep 'absent means JSON'). (2) Otherwise, if the declared return type is String and the Content-Type is text-class (text/*, application/xml, application/javascript, +xml) => the body string verbatim. (3) Otherwise => raise the SDK serialization error with a fixed message shape: "Unexpected response Content-Type '<media-type>' for <Class>.<operation>: expected a JSON body" (go: lowercase). Never a cast, never a silently returned raw string typed as a model, never a zero-valued model with a nil error, and never reuse the 'Expected a response body ... but received none' ApiError (that message stays for genuinely empty bodies). Void operations still ignore the body; binary returns follow the binary decision.
alternatives: Rejected: return the raw text typed as the model (python, ruby, node, php, elixir today): type confusion. Rejected: leave data null so the convenience method raises the empty-body ApiError (dart, rust, swift today): the message says 'received none' when a body was received. Rejected: sniff the body and parse JSON when it is mislabelled text/plain: a tolerant reader would silently accept protocol violations. Considered: return a zero value with no error (go today, locked by a go test): silent data loss.
rationale: (a) Precedent and spec: the OAS client convention (openapi-generator's own ApiClient.deserialize) is to throw 'Content type ... is not supported' unless the type is String; AGENTS error contract says a body that does not match the declared schema is a SerializationError (elixir already documents this in decode_success_body). (b) No current behaviour is a majority (5 different outcomes across 12), but 'raise' is what java/kotlin/csharp do accidentally (ClassCastException) and what the error contract asks for. (c) Safest for callers: the failure is loud, typed, names the offending header and keeps the response reachable. (d) Needs only a String type test that every language has (T::class == String::class, typeof(T)==typeof(string), return_type == 'str', 'String', 'String.t()', *string, etc.).

title: Binary request body with a non-binary Content-Type selected (setPetAvatar + application/json): send the caller's bytes verbatim, never re-encode
canonical: When the operation's request body parameter is format:binary (the generator knows this from the body param's isBinary), the SDK sends the caller-supplied bytes/stream/file UNCHANGED under whatever declared Content-Type the caller selected, including application/json. It never routes a binary body through the JSON serializer (no '{}', no base64 string, no int array, no reflected stream object). The selector therefore only changes the Content-Type header, as java/kotlin/rust/go comments already document; a caller who wants the {data,mimeType} envelope pre-builds the JSON and passes its bytes. The unrecognised-value rejection (AGENTS 'multi-consumes selector REJECTS an unrecognised value in all 12') is unchanged; application/json is a declared value and is accepted. Mechanism: the op template (which already reads bodyParam.isBinary) passes a rawBody flag to the shared invoke call; BaseApi's serialize ladder tests it first (after extractBinaryPart for the multipart Map case) so the clause cannot catch a legitimate format:byte JSON body in languages where binary and byte share a native type.
alternatives: Rejected: reject application/json when the body is binary. It makes a spec-declared request type unusable and still needs the same op-level flag. Rejected: generate an envelope body type or one parameter per content type (what F035 suggests): needs oneOf request bodies in all 12 codegens (L, and the JSON-vs-binary choice then cannot be a plain selector). Rejected: type-only pass-through in BaseApi (e.g. 'body is bytes'): python/node/dart/swift/elixir would then send format:byte JSON bodies raw instead of base64.
rationale: (a) The OAS media-type map pairs one schema per type; the SDK only models the first, so the honest behaviour is 'selector changes the header, body is the caller's'. (b) kotlin (body is ByteArray passthrough) and rust (body already bytes) already do exactly this; go/java/swift/python/node comments claim it. (c) The current outcomes are silent data loss ('{}' in java and go) or silent re-encoding (base64 string in python/swift/node, int array in dart); pass-through is loud at the server if the payload is wrong. (d) No dependency; one flag and one clause.

title: Multipart scalar parts: every primitive is a plain text part with the canonical stringify form; only objects/models are application/json parts
canonical: In multipart/form-data, a value that is a primitive (string, number, boolean, date, date-time, duration, uuid, enum) is written as a text part: Content-Disposition: form-data; name="x" and NO part Content-Type, its body being the SDK's ObjectSerializer.stringify form (the one already used for form-urlencoded, query and path values): true/false, 2024-01-15T10:30:00.000+00:00, 2024-01-15, red, 3. Only an object/model/map value is written as a JSON part with exactly Content-Type: application/json (no charset, no per-part Content-Length, header order Content-Disposition then Content-Type), serialized by the ObjectSerializer. Files keep the existing filename/MIME rules (the AGENTS closed 'multipart filename' decision is unaffected). An array of primitives repeats the text part per element.
alternatives: Rejected: JSON-encode non-string scalars as application/json parts (java, kotlin, csharp, php objects, node Date, go time, swift Date/enum, elixir DateTime today): the part body becomes a quoted string that no form parser accepts as a date. Rejected: language toString/interpolation (python was, ruby, go %v, csharp bool.ToString() = 'True', culture-sensitive floats). Considered: honour an explicit encoding.contentType on a primitive property as a JSON part (OAS allows it); not needed now and no spec in the repo declares it, so deferred.
rationale: (a) OAS 3.x Encoding Object: for a primitive property the default part Content-Type is text/plain, for an object application/json; RFC 7578 section 4.2 says a text field value is the plain string. (b) python and rust (op layer picks Text(stringify) vs Json) are already exactly this; php does it for is_scalar. (c) The JSON-part route silently adds quotes; interpolation silently changes format per language (csharp sends 'True'). (d) Every SDK already has stringify; no new dependency.
current_state: java: String/Number/Boolean text, everything else (OffsetDateTime, LocalDate, UUID, enum) a JSON part with Content-Type application/json and quoted body (DefaultApiClient.java:1088-1099). kotlin: same (DefaultApiClient.kt:476-499). csharp: string text; int/long/float/double/bool/decimal via value.ToString() so bool is 'True' and floats are culture-dependent (a gap the F254 finding missed); every other type a JSON part (DefaultApiClient.cs:869-905). php: is_scalar => ObjectSerializer::stringify (fixed, 'true'), but is_object catches DateTimeInterface and BackedEnum into JSON parts (DefaultApiClient.php:191 and :245, Psr18ApiClient.php:170 and :199). python: canonical, else-branch ObjectSerializer.stringify, models via ObjectSerializer.serialize (default_api_client.py:944-971). ruby: interpolates #{value} (Time => '2024-01-15 10:30:00 UTC') and to_hash => JSON (default_api_client.rb:572-588). node: typeof 'object' (Date, Temporal) => JSON part, primitives String(value) (abstract-api-client.ts:679-701). dart: String/num/bool toString, any other value jsonEncode (a DateTime throws JsonUnsupportedObjectError) (abstract_api_client.dart:639-657). go: string text, struct/map (time.Time, DateTime) JSON part, other fmt.Sprintf('%v') (base_api.go:462-512). rust: canonical, MultipartValue::Text(object_serializer::stringify(val)) vs Json chosen in the op layer (pet_api.rs:2849-2855, :387). swift: String/Bool/BinaryInteger/BinaryFloatingPoint interpolated text (fixed), Date/enum => application/json part (BaseApi.swift:476-499, DefaultApiClient.swift:497). elixir: binaries text, any map including DateTime/Date structs => JSON part, others to_string (default_api_client.ex:1090-1107).

title: Multipart JSON part headers: csharp/dart charset and header order, kotlin per-part Content-Length
canonical: A JSON part carries exactly Content-Disposition then Content-Type: application/json (no charset parameter, no per-part Content-Length). csharp and dart are fixed. Two residual library-forced differences are documented exceptions, not defects: (1) kotlin: Ktor's formData adds a Content-Length header to every binary part (RFC 7578 permits extra part headers and receivers must ignore them). (2) dart: a REPEATED text part (array of strings in multipart) must be added as an http.MultipartFile because MultipartRequest.fields is a Map<String,String> that cannot repeat a name, and package:http always emits a content-type (text/plain; charset=utf-8) for MultipartFile parts. Single text parts use fields and carry no content-type.
alternatives: Rejected: hand-build dart/kotlin multipart bodies to match byte-for-byte (L effort, replaces the platform multipart writers and their streaming/redirect-replay behaviour) for a header no server keys on.
rationale: csharp now builds the JSON part through CreateStringContent (DefaultApiClient.cs:369, :591 and the model branch near :895) which removes the charset/ordering difference; dart builds the JSON part with MultipartFile.fromBytes + MediaType('application','json') (abstract_api_client.dart:647-657) so no charset is added. What remains follows library behaviour (criterion d): Ktor's FormBuilder.append(ByteArray) adds Content-Length; package:http cannot repeat a field name without a file part.

title: x-www-form-urlencoded values: scalars use the canonical stringify form; nested objects/maps are rejected instead of emitting each language's repr
canonical: Every scalar field value in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body is encoded as ObjectSerializer.stringify(value) (canonical date, date-time, duration, uuid, enum, boolean forms), arrays of scalars repeat the key, null fields and null elements are omitted (all already true in 11 of 12 after the ruby fix). A value that is a model, map or array-of-objects has no defined encoding in the generator today (it does not emit the OAS encoding style/explode), so the SDK raises its serialization error ('form-urlencoded field <name> must be a scalar or array of scalars') instead of emitting java toString(), python str(), node '[object Object]', go %v, ruby to_s, rust compact JSON. Supporting OAS form/deepObject styles (reusing ValueSerializer.serializeStyled) is deferred until the generator surfaces the encoding block.
alternatives: Rejected: implement deepObject/form-explode now (the finding's proposal): requires the codegen to carry encoding.style/explode into every op template and a body-specific styled serializer in 12 languages (L) with no spec in the repo needing it. Rejected: keep the per-language repr: 12 different byte strings, none valid for a server.
rationale: (a) OAS only defines object encoding in form bodies through style/explode; an unqualified guess is not spec-conformant. (b) The scalar half is already majority-canonical and ruby now routes through ObjectSerializer.stringify (BaseApi.rb:267-278, with '*'/'~' normalised). (c) Failing loudly is the only choice that cannot put garbage on the wire. (d) A type guard needs no dependency.

risk: A spec that already has a nested object in a form body (none in this repo) will start failing at call time instead of sending a meaningless value. Deferred follow-up L: OAS encoding style support.

title: One value-preserving string-literal escaper per language for every spec string written into a code literal (defaults, server urls/variables, OAuth urls/scopes)
rationale: Criteria (a) and (c): a literal must evaluate to the spec bytes, and today ruby/php send `say \"hi\"` on the wire, newlines become spaces, and HTML entities replace `=`/`&` in operation-server URLs, all silent data changes. (b) java/kotlin/csharp/go/rust/swift/elixir already get quote and backslash right, so the fix is a shared escaper with per-language tables. (d) Needs no dependency. Root cause is shared by F045/F180 (defaults), F048/F176 (server literals, HTML escaping) and the unescaped scope/URL builders of F362. The StringBuilder-in-Java hygiene part of F362 is not parity and is excluded.

canonical: Contract: a string literal in generated source must evaluate to EXACTLY the spec's bytes. Add one overridable `escapeStringLiteral(String raw)` to AbstractBetterCodegen (body only, quotes stay in the template/caller) and expose it as `{{#lambda.stringLiteral}}{{{x}}}{{/lambda.stringLiteral}}`. Use it in every toDefaultValue string branch (replace escapeText), in every server/operation-server template (global: serverUrl, serverDescription, varDefault, varDescription, varEnumValues; operation: url, value), and in the OAuth builders (tokenUrl, refreshUrl, authorizationUrl, openIdConnectUrl, keyParamName, scope names; all 12 build*SuperArgs/format*Scopes). Rules: never escapeText, never escapeUnsafeCharacters (`*/` is harmless in a literal), never collapse newline/tab to a space, never HTML-escape (triple braces only; JMustache turns `=`, `&`, `'` into entities and changes wire bytes), never htmlUnescape (defaults, URLs, enum values are data; the existing preprocessOpenAPI comment already says so). Always escape backslash and the language's own quote character. Newline, CR, tab and other C0 controls use the language's escape. Neutralise the sigil only where that quote style interpolates: kotlin and dart `$` -> `\$`, elixir `#{` -> `\#{`. Swift `\(` is already safe because the backslash is doubled. ruby and php keep single-quoted literals where the ONLY escapes are `\\` and `\'`; a raw newline or tab stays literal inside the quotes (valid, exact). The wire value of a default or server URL is then identical in all 12.
alternatives: (1) Fix escapeText per language: rejected, it is a comment escaper and mutates by design (newline->space, `*/`, `\"` that single-quoted ruby/php keep literally). (2) Upstream escapeTextInSingleQuotes: rejected, it still collapses newlines and applies escapeUnsafeCharacters. (3) Warn or refuse hostile defaults: rejected, silently dropping a spec default is a silent data change. (4) Raw/verbatim strings (C# @"", Rust r#"", Python r''): rejected, not available or not safe in all 12. (5) Switch ruby/php to double-quoted to get \n: rejected, adds `$`/`#{`/`{$` interpolation hazards for no gain, since a literal newline inside single quotes is already exact. Does not contradict AGENTS.md (R7-6 unescapeDocComment only concerns prose in comments, covered by the next decision).

The StringBuilder-in-Java parts of F362 (ruby/python import and RBS builders) are code hygiene, not parity, and are NOT part of this decision: only the unescaped spec strings in those builders are.

title: Doc prose and package-manifest descriptions: one normalisation for comments, one escaper per manifest format
rationale: Criteria (a) and (c): prose must read as the spec says without HTML entities or broken comments, and each escaper must target the delimiter actually used. The current escapeUnsafeCharacters overrides target hazards that do not exist (python `'''`, ruby `=end`) and miss the real one (elixir `#{`). Manifests need the escaping of their own format (JSON/TOML/YAML-double-quoted share one rule, XML has lambda.escapeXml, three languages reuse the literal escaper). Consistent with AGENTS.md R7-6 (unescapeDocComment for doc prose). Feasible in all 12 with existing mechanisms.
current_state:
All three still true (templates unchanged). Prose from the spec reaches comments and manifests by different routes.
Tag and tag-externalDocs descriptions (AbstractBetterCodegen.injectTagMetadata ~4663) are stored raw; the other prose (operation notes, model description) goes through escapeText. Rendering of the raw tag text: java api.mustache:25, kotlin :25, php :26, go :74, ruby :78, elixir :75 use `{{{.}}}` (a multi-line value leaves bare code lines in go/ruby `//`/`#` comments; `*/` closes the java/kotlin/php block comment; `#{` interpolates in elixir `@moduledoc`); dart api.mustache:67, node apis.mustache:79, rust api.mustache:80 and swift api.mustache:55 use `{{.}}` which HTML-escapes already-unescaped text (`don't` -> `don't` in a comment); csharp :89 uses lambda.escapeXml (correct for XML doc, but newlines are not collapsed); python :75 is inside a docstring (only the closing triple quote can break it).
escapeUnsafeCharacters overrides: python (BetterPythonCodegen ~749) rewrites `'''` but no python template contains `'''` (grep finds none) so it only mangles prose; ruby (~829) rewrites `=begin`/`=end` (cannot occur at line start: escapeText collapses newlines) and `#{` -> `\#{`, which then LEAKS a backslash into `#` comments and single-quoted literals where `#{` is inert; elixir has no override and inherits only `*/`, so `Fetches /users/#{id}` in an operation description interpolates in `@doc` heredocs / `@moduledoc ".."` (elixir/api/api.mustache:23,99).
Manifests (`appDescription` is the escapeText'd info.description): node package.json (package.mustache:5), php composer.mustache:3, python pyproject_toml.mustache:4 and rust cargo_toml.mustache:7 use HTML-escaping `{{appDescription}}` (`Pets & owners'` is published as `Pets & owners'`); java pom.mustache:8 and csharp csproj.mustache:5 write it raw into XML (`&`/`<` makes the POM/csproj ill-formed); ruby gemspec.mustache:15 (`'..'`), kotlin build_gradle.mustache:19 (`".."`, `$` interpolates) and elixir mix_exs.mustache:44 (`".."`, `#{` interpolates) write it raw into a literal; dart pubspec.mustache:3-8 writes an unquoted YAML scalar (`: `, leading `&`/`*`/`#` break it). go/swift have no manifest description. Goldens show only the plain sentence (java pom.xml:8, node package.json:4, dart pubspec.yaml:3).
F048 doc copies: global server descriptions use `{{serverDescription}}` (HTML-escaped) in 10 comment sites; csharp now uses escapeXml (fixed); python servers.mustache:35-37 is raw inside a docstring.
canonical: Three contexts, three rules, no overlap with the literal escaper. (1) Doc-comment prose (tag, tag/op/model externalDocs, global server and server-variable descriptions, info): htmlUnescape once in preprocessOpenAPI (extend it to openAPI.getServers() and their variables, and to every ExternalDocumentation description; today it skips servers), then the same pipeline as operation notes: escapeText-style newline collapse, then escapeUnsafeCharacters, rendered with TRIPLE braces and with the same unescapeDocComment wrapper the language already uses for operation/model docs (go, dart, ruby). Never `{{ }}` for prose (HTML entities appear in comments). (2) escapeUnsafeCharacters is redefined as exactly the terminators/interpolators of the delimiters the templates really use for prose: java, kotlin, php, node, go (Servers `/* */`): `*/` -> `*_/` (kotlin also `/*` -> `/_*` because its block comments nest); csharp: lambda.escapeXml only; dart, rust, swift, ruby (`#`/`///`): identity; python: identity (escapeText already turned `"` into `\"`, so a triple quote cannot form); elixir: `#{` -> `\#{`. Delete the python and ruby overrides. (3) Manifest descriptions: expose a new plain `appDescriptionPlain` (htmlUnescaped info.description, whitespace runs collapsed to one space, NOT escapeText'd) and escape it for the manifest's syntax: package.json, composer.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml and pubspec.yaml (as a double-quoted scalar) use one `lambda.jsonString` (JSON, TOML basic strings and YAML double-quoted share \\ \" \n \uXXXX); pom.xml and csproj use lambda.escapeXml (exists); gemspec, build.gradle.kts and mix.exs use the previous decision's lambda.stringLiteral. The published description equals the spec text byte for byte.
alternatives: (1) Keep HTML-escaping manifests (`{{ }}`): rejected, it publishes entities to npm/PyPI/crates.io/Packagist and is only right for XML by accident. (2) Keep the cross-language `*/` guard on prose in languages that never use `/* */`: rejected, it alters glob examples like `src/**/*.ts` for no benefit. (3) Preserve multi-line prose in comments: rejected for now, the standing behaviour for all other prose is newline->space. (4) One generic Java escape function for all manifests: rejected, JSON/TOML/XML/Ruby/Kotlin/Elixir need different rules and lambdas keep the quotes in the template.
risk: Entity-decoded server and tag text now appears in comments, so goldens with `&`-style prose change (none today). Removing the python/ruby overrides changes any description containing `'''`, `=end` or `#{` from mangled to verbatim. Changing the info.description fixture re-renders every README/API-info/manifest; review the diff once.

title: Per-operation server codegen: one type per variable per operation, unique variant names
rationale: Criteria (b)/(c): all 12 emit the enum inside the variants loop, so any two variants sharing a variable break compilation in 8 languages and silently last-wins in 4 (python, ruby, php, and elixir under warnings). A variant must never accept a value its own server does not list, so merging value sets is rejected; keeping the existing name when the variable is unique avoids any golden churn. F122 and F145 are the same defect. Feasible in all 12 by computing names once in Java and iterating a per-operation list in the template.
current_state:
Both findings are the same defect and still true. AbstractBetterCodegen.enrichOperationServers (~4540-4620) builds serverVariables per variant and never de-duplicates; variantName = PascalCase(description with non-alphanumerics -> '_') else `Server<i>`, with no uniqueness or leading-digit check. Every template emits the variable enum inside `{{#variants}}{{#serverVariables}}{{#hasEnumValues}}` under a name that excludes the variant:
- java (api.mustache:52-71): nested `enum {{pascalName}}` twice -> duplicate member compile error (current golden shows the single case PetApi.java:134 `enum Region`).
- kotlin api.mustache, csharp api.mustache:36-37 (CS0101), dart api.mustache:33, rust api.mustache:42, swift api.mustache:18: duplicate type declarations, compile error.
- go api.mustache:36-44: `type {{serverTypeName}}{{pascalName}}` duplicate (golden pet_api.go:43-49 `GetMultiServerPetInfoServerRegion`); a description-only collision also duplicates the `...Server<Variant>` structs (pet_api.go:63-72).
- node apis.mustache:35: duplicate `export enum`.
- python api.mustache:39-44 and ruby api.mustache:25: silent re-definition, last one wins (wrong when enum sets differ).
- php server_variable_enum.mustache:11: same file written twice, last wins.
- elixir api.mustache:16: module redefinition, fatal under --warnings-as-errors.
Petstore getMultiServerPetInfo (openapi.yaml ~911-925) has only one variant with a variable, so nothing trips. Variant names from descriptions such as `1st region` or non-ASCII text become an invalid or empty identifier, and a variant named like a variable enum (`Region` vs `region`) collides with it in java/kotlin/csharp/swift.
canonical: Compute naming in enrichOperationServers and make every template emit enums from a per-operation list instead of per variant. (a) Variant names: PascalCase(description) as today, but fall back to `Server<index>` when the result is empty, does not start with a letter, or equals an earlier variant's name or any enum type name of the operation; if `Server<index>` would still collide, append the index. (b) Enum types: a variable name that appears in exactly ONE variant of the operation keeps the current name (`Region`, `Environment`; zero golden churn). If the same variable name appears in two or more variants of one operation, each variant's enum is named `<VariantName><Var>` (e.g. `RegionalRegion`, `MirrorRegion`), because their value sets may differ. Each enum is emitted exactly once, from a new `typeDef.serverEnums` list (typeName, varName, values, owning variant), and variants reference it by `enumTypeName`. Non-enum variables stay plain strings. Identical in all 12; php/python/ruby/elixir module and file names follow the same typeName.
alternatives: (1) Merge same-named variables into one enum with the union of values: rejected, a variant would silently accept values its server never declared (weakened validation). (2) Always prefix every enum with the variant name: rejected, renames every existing public type (Region -> RegionalRegion in all goldens) for no safety gain. (3) Emit only the first enum and ignore later ones: rejected, silent first/last-wins data change (what python/php/ruby do today). (4) Reject specs with duplicate variables: rejected, `https://{region}.a.com` + `https://{region}.b.com` is a normal multi-region pattern.
risk: Public type names change only for operations that already could not compile (java/kotlin/csharp/go/dart/rust/swift/node) or silently misbehaved (python/ruby/php/elixir). The YAML below renames the existing `Region` enum of getMultiServerPetInfo to `RegionalRegion` because the new Mirror variant shares `region`; the per-language PetApiTest templates that reference it must be updated.

title: Identifiers: a digit-leading or empty sanitised name gets a deterministic legal fallback, never an escape prefix
rationale: Criteria (a)-(c): the result must be a legal, public identifier in all 12 and must not drop data (go currently drops the property in both directions). No single punctuation prefix or suffix works everywhere (underscore is private in dart, rejected by pydantic, unexported in go, CA1707 in csharp), but a letter prefix does. Both findings are the same class: the sanitiser output is not a valid identifier. php already shows the right approach for whitespace-only enum values.
current_state:
Both still true (code unchanged: AbstractBetterCodegen.toVarName ~2236, toParamName ~2274, toEnumVarName ~2381-2405). A property or query param `2fa`/`1stPlace` is routed to escapeReservedWord, so the result is whatever each language's keyword escape does: java, kotlin, node, swift, ruby, elixir `_2fa` (legal); python `2fa_` (SyntaxError), dart `2fa_` (SyntaxError), php `$2fa_` (parse error), rust `r#2fa` (not a legal raw identifier), go `_2fa` (unexported struct field; the alias MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON, e.g. go/pkg/models/pet.go:114-125, skips it so the property is silently dropped both ways), csharp `_2fa` (CA1707 under the analyzers; BetterCSharpCodegen ~160 documents the rule). Dart also hits the same trap for digit-leading enum members: toEnumVarName returns `_` + name and a leading underscore is library-private in Dart.
Enum values: toEnumVarName strips the leading and trailing underscore after casing, so a value that is only spaces or symbols (`" "`, `@@`, non-ASCII without allowUnicodeIdentifiers) cleans to "" and the generated constant has an empty name -> compile error in 11 languages. Only BetterPHPCodegen.toEnumVarName (~694) maps whitespace-only to `SPACE_<n>`; nothing handles a collision after casing (`a-b` vs `a_b`). Not exercised: the petstore has no such property or enum value.
canonical: (1) Digit-leading variable/parameter name: prefix the LETTER `n` BEFORE applying the language casing (`2fa` -> `n2fa`; PascalCase csharp/go give `N2fa`; snake gives `n1st_place`). It must not go through escapeReservedWord. The wire name is already preserved by the serializer alias/tag. (2) Enum constant whose cleaned name is empty: whitespace-only -> `SPACE_<length>` (php's rule moved into the base), any other empty result -> `VALUE_<upper-hex codepoints joined by _>` (e.g. `@@` -> `VALUE_0040_0040`), then getEnumCasing; digit-leading enum names get the same letter prefix instead of `_`. (3) After the names of one enum are computed, a second constant with an identical name gets a `_2`, `_3` suffix in declaration order; wire values are untouched. All are pure functions of the value, so output is stable and identical across the 12.
alternatives: (1) Keep escapeReservedWord for digits and fix each override: rejected, no single punctuation prefix/suffix is legal in all 12. (2) Prefix `_` and special-case dart/python/go/csharp: rejected, more per-language exceptions and still unexported/private in go/dart. (3) Index-based enum fallback `VALUE_<i>`: rejected, toEnumVarName has no index and names would shift when a value is inserted. (4) Fail generation on unrepresentable values: rejected, dropping or aborting on a legal spec is worse than a deterministic name.
risk: Renames the public field/param for digit-leading names in java/kotlin/node/swift/ruby/elixir from `_2fa` to `n2fa` (rare). The enum collision suffix needs a hook after all enum var names exist (postProcessModelsEnum / property enum build): verify upstream DefaultCodegen does not already de-duplicate before writing it. A generated `n2fa` could collide with a real `n2fa` property; reuse the `_2` suffix logic if wanted.

title: Reserved-word escaping applies exactly to names the language cannot use (add java literals, narrow php/ruby)
rationale: Criterion (a) and (b): escape only what the language forbids, as swift, dart, go, csharp and node already do; java must also escape its literals, which are illegal identifiers. php keywords are legal `$property`/parameter names. kotlin soft-keyword escaping stays because AGENTS.md records it as a deliberate policy. Ruby and elixir narrowing is conditional on the golden's Steep/mix compile because RBS/atom handling of keyword names was not verified by reading.
current_state:
F309 is partly fixed: swift keeps `type` (swift Models/ApiResponse.swift:13 `public var type`), dart keeps `type`, `and`, `or`, `not` (BetterDartCodegen.shouldEscapeReservedVarName ~178; dart edge_cases.dart:21-29 shows `and`, `class_`, `return_`). Still over-broad: php escapes `and`/`or` to `$and_`/`$or_` (php Models/EdgeCases.php:36,39) but not `not` (`$not`, :42), and `class_`/`return_` (:45,48), although a keyword is a legal `$property`/parameter name and PHP 8 named arguments accept keywords; ruby `_and`, `_or`, `_not`, `_class`, `_return` (ruby models/edge_cases.rb:79-83), where only `class` really clashes (Object#class); elixir `_and`/`_or`/`_not` (elixir models/edge_cases.ex:47-49) while `class`/`return` are kept (inconsistent; unverified whether keyword atoms are usable). Correctly escaped real keywords: java/kotlin/swift `_class`/`_return`, python `class_`/`return_`, rust `r#return`. go/csharp/node never escape. kotlin escapes soft keywords by design (AGENTS.md: `file` -> `_file`, enforced by KotlinReservedWordsSpec).
F364 still true: reserved-words/java.txt contains no `true`, `false`, `null` (and no `_`, a keyword since Java 9), so a property `null` gives `public Boolean null;` (java models/EdgeCases.java:39-49 shows `and`/`or`/`not` plain, which is right). src/test/resources/scripts/JavaKeywords.java:20 explicitly excludes the literals and JavaReservedWordsSpec only checks the resource is a superset, so adding them is safe. csharp, dart, elixir, go, kotlin, node, ruby, rust, swift and python all list the literals; php does not (and does not need to for variables).
canonical: Escape an identifier only when the language cannot use it as a plain field/property/parameter name there. Concretely: (1) java.txt gains `true`, `false`, `null`, `_`, and JavaKeywords.java stops excluding the literals so JavaReservedWordsSpec enforces it. (2) php: `shouldEscapeReservedVarName` returns false for variable/property/parameter names (keep escaping `this`, and keep the list for class/method/const contexts), so `$and`, `$or`, `$class`, `$return` stay as written. (3) ruby: narrow the variable-escape set to identifiers that clash with Object/Kernel/Dry::Struct instance methods or cannot be a bare name (`class`, `self`, `nil`, `true`, `false`, `__FILE__`, ...) and drop `and`/`or`/`not`/`return` ONLY IF Steep and the RBS signature for `attribute :and` accept it in the ruby golden; otherwise document ruby `_and/_or/_not` as a FORCED exception in AGENTS.md. (4) elixir: same experiment for `and`/`or`/`not`; keep `_and` as a documented FORCED exception if the struct key or field access does not compile. (5) kotlin's soft-keyword escaping is a standing decision and stays.
alternatives: (1) Keep escaping every reserved word everywhere for predictability: rejected, it renames legal public fields (`$and_`) with no language feature forcing it, and swift/dart already moved away from it. (2) Remove the over-broad entries from the shared php.txt list: rejected, the same list guards class/method/constant names where keywords ARE illegal; use the var-name hook instead. (3) Escape java literals only for fields: rejected, they are illegal as any identifier.

title: Model names that collide with language or SDK types get the Model prefix in all 12, from a dedicated reserved-model-name set
rationale: Criteria (b)/(c): node already renames colliding models with `Model`, the other 11 either fail to compile (swift `Error`, rust `use super::*` with `Result`) or silently shadow a type the SDK uses. `Error`, `Date`, `Result` are very common schema names. A separate set is needed because languageSpecificPrimitives also drives import and primitive-vs-model decisions.
current_state: Still true: AbstractBetterCodegen.toModelName (~2216) applies getModelNameCollisionPrefix() only when it is non-empty and the PascalCase name is in languageSpecificPrimitives; only BetterNodeCodegen (~585) returns "Model". Per language today a schema named `Error`: swift shadows Swift.Error module-wide while the SDK uses it unqualified (swift DefaultApiClient.swift:723 `private struct UndecodableBody: Error`, SerializationError.swift:19 `cause: Error?`), so the SDK stops compiling; java/kotlin (`String`, `Object`, `Error`, `Exception` in the models package) shadow java.lang/kotlin types inside the package; php rejects `String`/`Null`/`True` etc. as class names; rust model files `use super::*` (rust src/models/pet_food.rs:8) so `Result`/`String`/`Option`/`Vec` shadow the prelude; dart `Error`/`List`/`Map`/`Type`; csharp `Task`/`Type`/`Enum`/`Exception`; python `Optional`/`List`/`Any` shadow typing imports; ruby `Types` (used by every model, `Types::Any`) / `Hash` / `Array`; go and elixir namespace models in their own package/module so only identifiers declared in the same package matter. java's languageSpecificPrimitives is only int/long/.../String/Object/byte[]/void (BetterJavaCodegen ~120), swift's is String/Bool/Int/Data/Date/UUID/Void/Any (~100), and these sets are also used for import decisions (BetterJavaCodegen ~1050-1067 etc.), so they cannot simply be extended.
canonical: Introduce a separate per-language `getReservedModelNames()` (prelude and builtin type names the generated source references unqualified, plus the SDK's own top-level type names in the same namespace) and make `getModelNameCollisionPrefix()` return "Model" in all 12 (node's existing convention, matching upstream openapi-generator's ModelError). toModelName checks the new set, not languageSpecificPrimitives, so import logic is untouched. Extend each set from the SDK's actual unqualified references (grep the golden).

title: String enum literals: escape the quote char (never strip it), escape backslash and interpolation sigils, in all 12
current_state:
Root: AbstractBetterCodegen.toEnumValue (AbstractBetterCodegen.java:2362) = quoteEnumValue(escapeEnumStringValue(v)); quoteEnumValue (:3894) deletes the quote char when shouldEscapeQuotationMark() is false. Nothing escapes a backslash, `$` or `#{`. Petstore enums only contain [a-z-] plus 'Available/Sold/on-hold', so nothing tests it.
java: "..." quote escaped as \", backslash NOT escaped (`a\d` fails to compile, `\u` hazards), value also lands in `{@code ...}` javadoc (model.mustache:23).
kotlin: same, plus `$eq` interpolates (model.mustache:97 @SerialName($eq) fails to compile).
csharp: own table getEnumStringEscapes (BetterCSharpCodegen.java:622): \n \t \r and a lookbehind rule for `"`; backslash not escaped.
python: single-quoted, shouldEscapeQuotationMark=false (BetterPythonCodegen.java:737) so `o'clock` becomes 'oclock' (wire value silently changed); backslash unescaped (`a\b` = backspace).
ruby: same strip (BetterRubyCodegen.java:817).
php: same strip (BetterPHPCodegen.java:688).
dart: same strip (BetterDartCodegen.java:298); `$eq` interpolates (dart/models/model.mustache:29).
node: single-quoted, DOES escape `'` as \' (default true) but not backslash.
go: double-quoted, `"` escaped, backslash not.
rust: same as go; value is in #[serde(rename = ...)] (rust/models/model.mustache:31).
swift: same as go; `\(` in a value would start an interpolation.
elixir: same as go; `#{x}` interpolates (elixir/models/model.mustache:33,49).
canonical: The enum literal emitted into source must evaluate, in the target language, to EXACTLY the spec string. Implemented once in AbstractBetterCodegen.escapeEnumStringValue (default body, run before quoteEnumValue), in this order: (1) `\` -> `\\`; (2) the language quote char -> `\<q>` (delete every shouldEscapeQuotationMark()=false override so quoteEnumValue escapes instead of strips); (3) CR/LF/TAB -> `\r` `\n` `\t` in every language EXCEPT ruby and php, whose single-quoted literals interpret only `\\` and `\'` (a raw newline is legal there and `\n` would be a literal backslash-n); (4) interpolation neutralisation via getEnumStringEscapes: kotlin `$`->`\$`, dart `$`->`\$`, elixir `#{`->`\#{`. swift `\(` is covered by (1). Nothing else is rewritten. Where the raw value is echoed in a doc comment (java `{@code ...}` model.mustache:23/67/110, go `/* ... */` model.mustache:24, dart/rust `///`), render a comment-safe variant (apply escapeUnsafeCharacters so `*/` cannot close the comment) rather than the code literal.

(d) Every language has a valid escape (\' in python/dart/php/ruby/node, \$ in kotlin/dart, \#{ in elixir), so nothing is forced. Then expand with the OAS rows, scalar leaves via the canonical stringify: query form+explode(default) `k1=v1&k2=v2` (keys NOT prefixed by the param name); query form+explode=false `name=k1,v1,k2,v2` (one param, same comma-then-percent-encode path the array form/no-explode branch already uses); deepObject `name[k]=v` (extend serializeDeepObject to accept the converted map); header/path simple `k1,v1,k2,v2` and simple+explode `k1=v1,k2=v2`. A NESTED object or array leaf has no OAS serialization and raises the SDK SerializationError (never stringified, never dropped). spaceDelimited/pipeDelimited on an object also raise SerializationError. rationale: (a) OAS 3.x defines these rows explicitly. (c) Today three of the failure modes are compile errors (java, kotlin, csharp, rust) or silent drops (go, swift), and node/elixir send wrong keys; a compile error breaks the whole SDK for any spec with a model-typed deepObject, which is common in real specs. title: Reject a path parameter value of exactly '.' or '..' before dispatch, in all 12
current_state:
No SDK rejects or encodes dot segments (grep of the 12 goldens finds none; only php AbstractApiClient.php:555 mentions dot segments, for redirect resolution). All 12 encodePathSegment keep `.` literal (java ValueSerializer.java:117, python value_serializer.py:102, node value-serializer.ts:210, go value_serializer.go:79, rust value_serializer.rs:26, kotlin ValueSerializer.kt:100, csharp ValueSerializer.cs:89, php ValueSerializer.php:133, swift ValueSerializer.swift:62, ruby value_serializer.rb:87, elixir value_serializer.ex:106, dart value_serializer.dart). getPetByName("..") builds /pet/byName/..?category=x. What happens next is transport dependent. Verified locally: node WHATWG URL -> http://h/pet/?x=1 (even %2e%2E is normalised), python urllib3 2.6.3 parse_url -> /pet/?x=1, swift URL(string:) keeps `..` literally (only .standardized collapses it). From the finding, not run here: dart Uri.parse collapses it (reroutes), rust url crate / csharp System.Uri / php Symfony resolve most likely collapse it; java.net.URI and ruby send it literally; go net/http and elixir most likely send it literally.
So java/swift/ruby/go/elixir send /pet/byName/.. while node/python/dart(/rust/csharp/php) silently hit /pet/.
canonical: A path parameter whose final simple-style value is exactly `.` or `..` is rejected client-side, before any request, with the SDK's existing argument error, message `Path parameter '<name>' must not be '.' or '..'` (go lowercases `path`). It sits next to, and is raised from the same place as, the existing empty-path rejection: the serializer's path check in the 10 languages that have one; the operation-layer path guard in rust and swift (whose serializers have no path guard, AGENTS R6-5/R8-6). Percent-encoded forms need no rule: a literal `%2E%2E` input is encoded to `%252E%252E`. Matrix/label styles prefix their value (`;n=..`, `...`) so they can never be a dot segment. Substrings such as `a..b` or `.hidden` are untouched.
rationale: (c) A user-controlled name can silently re-route the request to a different endpoint (/pet instead of /pet/byName/..) in at least 3 SDKs; encoding cannot fix it because WHATWG parsers (node, rust) resolve even %2E%2E, so only rejection is uniform. (a) RFC 3986 section 5.2.4 treats `.`/`..` segments as path navigation, so they are not addressable resource identifiers. (d) trivial in every language (same shape as the existing empty check). Not forced anywhere.
alternatives: Rejected: always encode `.` as %2E (node and rust still normalise it; 10 languages change bytes for nothing). Rejected: fix only the three transports that normalise (leaves java/swift/ruby/go/elixir sending a dot-segment that a proxy or server will resolve).
risk: Low. A resource whose id is literally `.` or `..` could never be reached through a URL path anyway. Over-strictness only if a template is `/x/{a}.{b}` with a='.'; the check is on the standalone value so this is not hit.

title: allowReserved: leave literal only the RFC 3986 query-legal reserved set; percent-encode '#', '[' and ']' in all 12; document the WHATWG/URI-class '''' rewrite as FORCED in node, rust, ruby
current_state:
All 12 encode_query_allowing_reserved keep `: / ? # [ ] @ ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =` literal (e.g. node value-serializer.ts:252-270, java ValueSerializer.java:177-199, python value_serializer.py:142 safe="/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;=:"). The transport then rewrites URLs. Wire result of a value with `[ ] ' #`:
java: java.net.URI keeps all literal, a literal `#` becomes the URI fragment and is NOT sent (query truncated).
kotlin: Ktor keeps literal; `#` truncates (same).
csharp: System.Uri keeps `[ ] '`; `#` truncates.
python: urllib3 2.6.3 parse_url (default_api_client.py:446) re-encodes `[`/`]` to %5B/%5D (verified locally), keeps `'`; `#` -> fragment.
ruby: after the QueryParamsEncoder fix (default_api_client.rb:67-81) reserved chars survive Faraday's Hash round trip, but Faraday Request#url slices at `#` and URI::Generic#query= escapes `'` to %27 and `#` to %23 (verified on ruby 2.6.10); `[ ]` stay literal.
node: WHATWG URL (fetch) rewrites `'` to %27 (verified locally), keeps `[ ]`; `#` -> hash, truncates.
php: nyholm/psr7 filterQueryAndFragment (composer.json:33) encodes `[ ]` (likely, not run), keeps `'`.
dart: Uri.parse (abstract_api_client.dart:167) encodes `[ ]` to %5B/%5D (finding; not run here).
go: net/url keeps RawQuery as given.
rust: reqwest::Url::parse (default_api_client.rs:226) WHATWG special-query set rewrites `'` to %27.
swift: URL(string:) (DefaultApiClient.swift:207) encodes `[ ]` to %5B/%5D (verified locally on macOS).
elixir: keeps literal.
Net: `[ ]` literal in java/kotlin/csharp/go/elixir/node/ruby but %5B%5D in python/dart/swift/php; `'` literal in 9 and %27 in node/rust/ruby; a literal `#` silently truncates the query in every SDK. petstore only tests v1.0/beta:rc1, and only at encoder level.
canonical: allowReserved leaves literal exactly the characters RFC 3986 section 3.4 permits in a query component: `: / ? @ ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =` (plus unreserved `A-Za-z0-9-._~`). It always percent-encodes `#` (%23), `[` (%5B) and `]` (%5D), and everything else (space -> %20, controls, non-ASCII) as before. The encoder output is the contract: it is what the SDK hands the transport. FORCED exception, documented in AGENTS.md: node (WHATWG URL), rust (url crate, WHATWG) and ruby (URI::Generic#query=) turn a literal `'` into %27 after the SDK encodes; the other 9 send `'` literally. A server decodes both identically; do not try to defeat the URL parsers.
rationale: (c) A literal `#` can never be on the wire inside a query: every URL parser treats it as the fragment delimiter, so allowReserved values containing `#` silently lose the rest of the query today in all 12; that is silent data loss. (a) RFC 3986 section 3.4 does not allow `[ ]` in a query; OAS lists them but they cannot be honoured in dart (Uri) and swift (URL) without abandoning the platform URL types, and python/php already normalise them, so encoding them is the only value reachable in all 12 without a new dependency (criterion d). Making the encoder match what 4 transports already produce moves 7 languages to the same bytes and changes nothing for the 4. For `'` the criteria say document, not force (instruction d): 9 of 12 keep it literal and the OAS text allows it.

canonical: Every content: application/json query parameter value is produced by the same function that serializes request bodies (java/kotlin objectSerializer.serialize, csharp Serializer.Serialize, python self._object_serializer.serialize, ruby/node/php ObjectSerializer.serialize, dart serialize, go serialize(), rust object_serializer::serialize, swift ObjectSerializer.serialize, elixir ObjectSerializer.serialize), and any failure propagates as the SDK SerializationError (swift `try` not `try?`, go/rust return the error instead of discarding it). The resulting compact JSON text (no spaces, `/` and non-ASCII unescaped, `<` unescaped, canonical date-time +00:00, wire property names) is then percent-encoded by the normal query encoder.

(c) Today a failure either sends an empty string (rust), drops the param (swift) or raises a foreign type (elixir); bytes differ for `<`, `/`, non-ASCII, dates. (d) every SDK already has the function, nothing new is needed; none of the 8 bypasses is forced.

risk: Low; only content-typed query params are affected and petstore has none. csharp: BaseApi.Serializer is private (BaseApi.cs:28), make it protected/internal or add a BaseApi helper. Only application/json is in scope; other content media types stay unsupported.

title: format: byte parameters (query, header, path, form) are base64-encoded, in all 12
current_state:
No SDK has a byte branch on the parameter path (grep isByteArray in api templates: none; only dart/elixir model templates use it), although model bodies already round-trip base64 in all 12 (AGENTS R8-1). For bytes "hi":
java: String.valueOf(byte[]) -> `[B@6d06d69c` (ObjectSerializer.java:195).
kotlin: ByteArray.toString() -> `[B@...` (ObjectSerializer.kt stringify else-branch :540).
csharp: byte[] is an IList so ValueSerializer.cs:50 treats it as an array -> `104,105` (or p=104&p=105 exploded); Stringify falls to ToString (ObjectSerializer.cs:148).
python: str(b'hi') -> `b'hi'` (object_serializer.py:591).
node: Buffer -> String(value) (object-serializer.ts:789) raw bytes as text.
ruby: String#to_s raw bytes (param type is String with format byte, binary_vault.rb:54).
php: ?string raw bytes (php stringify :255-300).
dart: Uint8List is a List -> `104,105` (value_serializer.dart:453).
go: toStringSlice reflects over []byte -> `104,105` (value_serializer.go:406).
rust: Vec<u8> through serde -> `[104,105]` (object_serializer.rs:430).
swift: Data.description -> `2 bytes` (ObjectSerializer.swift:301).
elixir: binary sent raw (object_serializer.ex stringify).
canonical: A parameter declared type: string, format: byte (and each element of an array/map of them) serializes to standard-alphabet RFC 4648 base64 WITH padding (`aGk=` for "hi") before the normal query/header/path/form encoding (so the query wire is `aGk%3D`, header `aGk=`). Two mechanisms, one result: (1) the nine languages whose native byte type is distinct (java byte[], kotlin ByteArray, csharp byte[], python bytes, node Buffer/Uint8Array, dart Uint8List, go []byte, rust Vec<u8>, swift Data) get a byte branch at the TOP of the central stringify/serialize-styled dispatch, before any IList/List/slice/array check; (2) php, ruby and elixir model byte as a plain string/binary, so the type cannot tell bytes from text: the API templates wrap the value with the language's base64 encoder when the parameter has isByteArray (and items.isByteArray), using one helper per language (ObjectSerializer.encodeBase64Param). A null stays omitted.
rationale: (a) OAS `format: byte` means base64 text, and the SDKs already apply that to bodies; (c) the current outputs are identity hashes, comma lists or raw binary, i.e. silently wrong data; (d) every language has a stdlib base64 encoder. Type-driven stringify for the nine is one function per language instead of four template sites; the three string-typed languages cannot be type-driven without corrupting genuine text params, hence the codegen flag.
alternatives: Rejected: param-driven wrap in all 12 (4 call-site families x 12 templates, easy to miss header/path/form; the typed nine are fixed centrally by one branch). Rejected: reject byte params (valid OAS, simple to support). Rejected: URL-safe base64 (OAS format byte is the standard alphabet).
risk: php/ruby/elixir callers who today pass an already-base64 string would be double-encoded: the Options field doc must say the value is the raw bytes. Latent today (petstore has no byte param), and the current output was never usable. Kotlin/csharp/go/dart ordering matters: the byte branch must precede the collection branch.

canonical: Wire order = declaration order: query params in the operation's parameter order, form-urlencoded pairs and multipart parts in the request-body schema's property order, with array members expanded in place in array order; authenticator-contributed query params (apiKey in query) are appended after the operation's own params.
